title: Peasants' Revolt sources sheet
subject: History
unit: Summer 1: Medieval peasants and the Black Death (Peasants, Princes & Pestilence)
source: Written for history/y5 lesson 20 (Peasants' Revolt sources sheet (portal printable; teacher-written summaries of chronicle accounts, not quotations; assessed))
intro: Lesson 20: The Peasants' Revolt, 1381. Read the ideas from the lesson, then do the tasks.

panels.title: Source A: summary of a monk's chronicle written soon after 1381
panels.text: The writer describes the rebels as wicked men who burned the houses of the king's officials in London. He says they were angry about the new poll tax, which every adult had to pay, and that they wanted to kill the advisers they blamed for it.

panels.title: Source B: summary of a sermon by the priest John Ball, as reported by chroniclers
panels.text: John Ball told the crowds that all people were equal at the beginning of the world and that no one should be a serf. He said the time had come for ordinary people to be free of their lords.

panels.title: Causes
points: Fewer workers after the Black Death

timeline.label: 14 June
timeline.text: King meets rebels at Mile End

parts.text: Who: a monk, writing soon after
But: monks were often on the lords' side
Useful for events, careful with opinions

keywords.def: when people rise up against rulers
a tax that everyone pays the same
something from the past that gives evidence
someone who fights against those in power

questions.q: How old was Richard II in 1381?
Give one cause of the revolt.
questions.a: Poll tax, low wages law, villein work

questions.q: Core (assessed source question): Read the two sources on the sheet. In the portal response box answer: 'What do these sources tell us about why the peasants revolted?' Use: 'Source A shows... Source B suggests...'
questions.a: Uses both sources: poll tax anger and wanting freedom; notes who wrote each

questions.q: Extend: Was the revolt a success? Give one yes and one no.
questions.a: Yes: no similar poll tax for a long time, wages rose; No: promises broken, Tyler killed

questions.q: Stretch: Why might a chronicle writer be against the rebels?
questions.a: Writers were often monks or friends of lords, who lost out

questions.q: The poll tax was unfair because:
questions.a: B) Everyone paid the same. Rich and poor paid the same amount, which hit the poor hardest.

questions.q: Big question: is it ever right to rise up against unfairness?
questions.a: A reasoned view, e.g. speak up peacefully first; injustice must be challenged
